criteria.criterion: Git::exit, the gitleaks runner's run, and the xtask policy.rs git() helper no longer write all stdin before reading stdout; stdin is written on a separate thread (or equivalent concurrent drain).
criteria.evidence: Read the diff. In crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs, Git::exit now calls output_with_stdin, which writes stdin inside std::thread::scope while the main thread runs child.wait_with_output(). In crates/athena-gate/src/secrets.rs, Gitleaks::run calls athena_git::output_with_stdin. In xtask/tests/policy.rs (lines 35-45), git() writes stdin on a scoped thread while wait_with_output drains stdout.

criteria.criterion: The athena-git and athena-gate call sites share one helper; xtask uses it or a documented local equivalent if using it would alter the crate dependency graph.
criteria.evidence: Both crates call the public helper athena_git::output_with_stdin. xtask has a local copy, and a comment at policy.rs:32-34 says xtask may not depend on athena-git under the architecture policy and that this code mirrors the helper. The CHANGELOG entry records the same reason.

criteria.criterion: A write error from a child that exits early (broken pipe) is handled without panic or hang.
criteria.evidence: The helper ignores ErrorKind::BrokenPipe and returns any other write error only after waiting for the child. The xtask copy discards the write result. The test a_child_that_exits_without_reading_is_not_an_error runs `sh -c 'exit 3'` with 3 MB of input; it passed, returning Ok with exit code 3.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test` from the repo root: a new test piping more than 1 MB through an echoing child (e.g. cat) passes, and xtask policy tests complete rather than hang.
criteria.evidence: piping_over_a_megabyte_through_an_echoing_child_does_not_deadlock (3 MB through cat) passed. The xtask policy suite ran 9 tests, all passing, in 5.01 s. The full workspace `cargo test -q` reported no failures in any test binary.

criteria.criterion: `cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
criteria.evidence: Both commands exited 0 with no warnings or diffs. Athena's own run of clippy with --locked -D warnings and fmt --all --check also passed.

findings.summary: The same write-all-stdin-then-read pattern remains in other places that pipe stdin.
findings.evidence: claude.rs writes the whole user prompt to the child's stdin before starting the stdout reader thread. binary.rs writes the hook event before wait_with_output. Both are low-risk: the hook reads all its input before writing, and claude -p reads the prompt before producing output. But the request called this pattern the root cause at 'every place that pipes input to a child'. Moving these to the helper, or to a stdin-writer thread, would be a small follow-up.

findings.summary: If the writer thread panics, the panic is silently treated as a successful write.
findings.evidence: `writer.join().unwrap_or(Ok(()))` swallows a panic from the writer thread. write_all should not panic, so this is unlikely to matter.

summary: The change fixes the deadlock at all three places the user named. It adds `athena_git::output_with_stdin`, which writes stdin on a scoped thread while `wait_with_output` drains stdout and stderr. A broken pipe is ignored; any other write error is returned. `Git::exit` and `Gitleaks::run` now both call this helper. The xtask `git()` test helper has a commented local copy of the same approach, because xtask may not depend on athena-git. A new test pipes 3 MB through `cat` and passes; this would deadlock with the old write-everything-first pattern. A second test covers a child that exits without reading its input. I ran the new tests, `cargo test -p xtask` (the 9 policy tests finished in about 5 s), the full `cargo test`, clippy with `-D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --check`. All passed. One minor follow-up: the same write-then-read pattern still exists in `crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs` and `crates/athena-cli/tests/binary.rs`. It is unlikely to cause trouble there today, and the accepted reading limited the job to the three named sites. The xtask/Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock and docs/architecture.md files listed as deliverables were left unchanged, which fits the local-fix route the reading allowed.
